# ECN-2026-015 - Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Related documents: ECN-2026-002, SOP-P1-L4-02, SOP-P1-L4-04

Reason for change
-----------------

This engineering change notice documents a modification to the operational control for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3, EQ-P1-L4-HT03. The change corrects an identified risk condition in the post-soak transfer-to-quench sequence that can result in unacceptable microstructural variability for affected forgings. Root-cause analysis referenced in ECN-2026-002 identified a timing allowance in the control recipe that exceeded the process window validated in initial qualification. The immediate objective is to impose a firm maximum on the delay between furnace extraction and immersion quench to align operation with metallurgical acceptance criteria and to close the procedural gap in SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-04.

The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds.

Background and rationale
------------------------

During routine quality trend reviews and verification sampling, a pattern of elevated hardness scatter was traced to inconsistent heat transfer during the transfer-to-quench interval. Metallurgical evaluation showed that delays beyond the validated transfer window increase the risk of undesirable transformation products. The control change is limited to EQ-P1-L4-HT03 and targets the control logic, operator procedures, and acceptance criteria recorded on shift logs and process control records.

This change follows the scope and intent of ECN-2026-002 and supplements procedural revisions in SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-04. The approach balances production continuity against the need to mitigate nonconforming output: hardware remains unchanged; software and procedural constraints are adjusted to enforce the revised timing limit.

Affected items
--------------

- All work orders processed on EQ-P1-L4-HT03 while performing heat treat recipes that require immersion quench.  
- Operator checklists and control-panel prompts associated with SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-04 when executed on EQ-P1-L4-HT03.  
- Shift logs, nonconformance logs, and process control records generated during the transfer-to-quench operation for EQ-P1-L4-HT03.

Affected deliverables that must be updated in the document control system:
- SOP-P1-L4-02 (operational sequence) — update to incorporate enforced transfer-to-quench timing and revised operator actions when the limit is reached.
- SOP-P1-L4-04 (sampling and verification) — update to include additional sampling triggers and disposition steps when transfer delay exceeds the allowable maximum.

Implementation
--------------

Scope of implementation
- The change applies only to EQ-P1-L4-HT03 in Plant P1, line P1-L4 and to operators and technicians authorized on that equipment.

Control logic update
- Update the furnace control recipe to enforce the maximum transfer-to-quench delay as specified above. The control system shall inhibit further soak timer progression that would permit a transfer delay beyond the stated maximum and shall generate an alarm and hold the workflow for operator intervention if the limit is reached.

Operator procedure updates
- Revise SOP-P1-L4-02 to include: pre-transfer confirmation steps, real-time monitoring of transfer initiation, actions to take when an alarm is triggered, and required notifications to supervision.
- Revise SOP-P1-L4-04 to include: sampling frequency adjustments for the first production run after implementation, the required hardness and microstructure verification samples to validate the effect of the change, and disposition paths for suspect material.

Training and competency
- Conduct targeted training on the revised SOPs and control actions for all personnel assigned to EQ-P1-L4-HT03 prior to the change going live. Training records must be retained in the training management system and cross-referenced to the shift coverage record.

Operational exceptions and contingencies
- If the control alarm is received indicating the delay limit is reached, operators shall follow the exception workflow in SOP-P1-L4-02, secure the affected load, and initiate the corrective sample sequence per SOP-P1-L4-04. No product shall be released from EQ-P1-L4-HT03 without completion of the disposition path specified in SOP-P1-L4-04.

Verification and validation
- Execute one monitored production run under the revised control with full metallurgical verification per SOP-P1-L4-04. Maintain verification records, including the transfer-to-quench timing capture, process parameters, and sample results, in the process control folder for the lot.

Records to keep
---------------

Maintain the following records in the equipment file and quality system for traceability:
- Control system configuration change log for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 (including reason for change and person authorizing the change).
- Operator training sign-off records for the revised SOPs.
- Alarm and event logs showing any instances where the transfer-to-quench delay reached the maximum and subsequent actions taken.
- Process verification records and metallurgical sample results created during the initial implementation run and for subsequent verification runs as required by SOP-P1-L4-04.
- Disposition records for any affected forgings that fail verification.

Examples of documented entries
- Example entry in the shift log: description of alarm condition, start of hold, sample initiation per SOP-P1-L4-04, supervisory notification, outcome of verification testing, and final disposition.
- Example entry in the nonconformance log: reference to work order, identification of failed sample, corrective action taken, and link to control configuration change.

Approvals
---------

Approval of this ECN authorizes the changes described herein for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 and requires coordinated updates to SOP-P1-L4-02 and SOP-P1-L4-04 prior to live operation. Approval signatories shall confirm completion of control changes, training, and initial verification records before the revised process is placed back into production.

Related documents: ECN-2026-002, SOP-P1-L4-02, SOP-P1-L4-04

(End of document)
